provenance.method: Smallest footprint first, per snapshot: the satellite-cell pairs in view are filled in 40 geometric footprint bands from the smallest, 4 proportional passes in each, every band committed before the next; per satellite at most its beams, per cell one co-channel layer (its area) and the class's people cap, per pair one layer: the phone class's allocation, and each directional class's first layer at its own people cap. A directional class then stacks layers under sky sectors: its terminal's sky above the mask split into sectors of equal solid angle, ring by ring from the zenith; a second banded fill on the same band edges over (cell, sector) keys, a key's area the cell's less its first layer's from that sector, a pair's cap one layer less its first-layer beams; before each band its candidates are taken by (cell, footprint, satellite), and one is admitted only at least one terminal beamwidth, sqrt(4 pi / (1.133 x D)), from every satellite serving its cell in another sector and from every candidate of its cell admitted earlier in the band in another sector (a satellite serves a cell when its layer covers at least 1 / SINR_1 of it). Each served sub-pair is priced by the full sum of its cell's other layers in other sectors (first layers not against each other), each weighted by its share of the cell at the terminal's Gaussian main lobe floored at -20 dB: SE = 0.65 x log2(1 + SINR), the single-layer SINR_1 = 2^(central SE / that anchor) - 1; a cell keeps its stacked layers only when they do not lower its capacity, the dropped beams spent. Each directional row reports its kept stacked share (the share of L in the kept stacked sub-pairs, in cells their first layer covers, that the full sum prices against a layer of another sector), their beam-weighted median separation from the nearest such layer and their beam-weighted mean full-sum interference in dB, none of them measured against the cell's main satellite alone. A circular Walker Delta shell at 450 km and 53 degrees (P = round(sqrt(N)) planes of S = round(N / P), the realized N = P x S, phasing F = 1) with a 25 degree mask; a square 25 m^2 aperture at 1.621 GHz, half-power beamwidth 0.886 wavelengths over its side, the beams per satellite derived from the capacity calibration and the panel. Each fleet's row averages its snapshots, drawn once over a sidereal day from seed 20260928. Maximum use in closed form (every cell served by the best satellite the shell can ever offer it; for a directional class one layer per sky sector, each at the best its ring allows, whether its azimuth is reachable ignored); the markers on the elasticity of capacity at the geometric midpoints of the rows, interpolated in ln N. The phone class's central rows carry the interference trim, priced on the first 1 snapshot(s) of each row: power control gives every beam equal flux at its target, so a beam's power goes as its slant range squared over g, g = cos^1.3 of its scan angle; a victim cell's aggregate far-sidelobe interference over its own signal is x = gamma / G0 x the sum, over every lit satellite above the victim's horizon, of the satellite's summed beam powers x g toward the victim / the slant range squared, G0 the panel's broadside directivity (4 pi x its area / the wavelength squared); 3,000 served cells are the victims, drawn without replacement in proportion to their beams, a fresh draw from seed 11 at each row; the trim is 1 - the victims' mean of log2(1 + 1 / (1 + x)), at each floor gamma of -0.4, -2, -8 dBi. Each band point of the phone class is its central curve but for one changed input, at 2 snapshot(s) a row over the same fleets, with its own rows and markers: the beam's half-power width (the taper), the ground a co-channel beam occupies over its 3 dB footprint (wider co-channel spacing, scaling the area per beam in the fill, the bounds and maximum use alike), the demand threshold, the grid (the shipped cells summed k x k), or the beams per satellite.
checks_passed: bounds: at every snapshot of every class and band point, useful beams at most min(ceiling, supply) and the ceiling at most maximum use (for a directional class, the sector-rule ceiling and its maximum use), within 1e-09 relative
stall floor: from 20,000 satellites up, the phone class's central useful beams at least 0.98 x min(ceiling, supply), at every snapshot and in the snapshot means
capacity per satellite never rises between consecutive rows of any class or band point by more than 0.02 relative to the earlier row (the snapshots' noise)

limits: Fluid (fractional) beams, idealized 3 dB footprints and one circular shell.
Residential (night-time) population, every place at its busy hour at once.
No terrain or building blockage, and no interference from other systems.
Take-up 1 is the maximal-demand bound: the capacity found is assumed used. The fluid model credits a beam hanging over a coast with its land share only (the coastal under-credit).
Computed with the band in full-time use (d = 1): the engine scales people and capacity by the downlink share d, and so ignores how d relaxes each cell's people cap inside the curve (ADR 008).
No interference trim for the directional classes: each terminal's own pattern suppresses the far-sidelobe leak.
The directional terminals' pattern floor (-20 dB) is an estimate, optimistic for the small terminal.

Computed at the 25 m^2 reference panel. The engine scales the curve linearly by the scenario's panel over it: below it the directional classes carry more than the rule gives, because their people caps do not shrink with the panel; the rule is exact in beams for the phone class; and each beam's rate is held at its reference-panel value, so the link effect of another array size is not modeled.
